title: Capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations: EEG data from Experiment 2
description: EEG recordings from 24 participants viewing static images of moving and non-moving, natural and artificial objects. The study tests whether capacity for movement is an organisational principle in object representations, separate from aliveness or animacy. Participants completed a speeded classification task and a passive rapid serial visual presentation task. The dataset includes raw BrainVision data, preprocessed derivatives, decoding results, analysis code, and 400 CC0 stimulus images.
methods_description: Participants completed two tasks while EEG was recorded. In the classification task they judged single images as 'can move' or 'still', with a 1 second timeout per trial. In the passive viewing task they watched rapid serial visual presentation streams of images and pressed a button when the fixation cross changed colour. Raw data are in BrainVision format. Preprocessed data are in EEGLAB and CoSMoMVPA formats.
